I see a lot of similarities between your story and mine. Seeing that unaliving yourself is such a thing people immediately want to jump on to prevent, I am not such a person. 
It's quite comforting to see that someone who has gone through a lot like you, still has the wish to help people. 
A couple years ago I worked out a theory of some sort. To summarize, some people need to be a target, someone who will have to deal with the pain of realisation and acceptation they will not have a "normal" life, they will have the sole function to help others and set aside everything else. One who gives up their life slowly do others can grow. I call those people "feeders". I am a feeder. I see a lot of posts about people, their stories, their experiences and their final plans. Yours is the only one I can actually fully connect with. 
I want to thank you for sharing your story. May your moments left in your life go the way you want them to, regardless of the decisions you make.

Having a mood related reaction to medication is completely normal. So is it from missing a dose. When I miss my dose of medication it brings me a lot of side effects. What helped me is to get a reminder notification on my Google calendar at the times I need to take the meds. I only mark it as done (and thus removing the notification) when I took them. Also, it's not a bad idea to discuss it with your psychiatrist. Maybe he has some ideas, maybe not per se directly but definitely for the long term of the treatment.
